Loggers

Source: R/log_logger.R
loggers.Rd

log_call() hands each message to a logger. A logger is an S7 object that inherits from logger_base, and logger_fn() decides how it is written.

Usage

logger_base(
  trace = "TRACE",
  debug = "DEBUG",
  info = "INFO",
  warn = "WARN",
  error = "ERROR",
  fatal = "FATAL",
  threshold = "info",
  logger = NULL
)

logger_fn(class, level, msg, ...)

logger_message(
  trace = "TRACE",
  debug = "DEBUG",
  info = "INFO",
  warn = "WARN",
  error = "ERROR",
  fatal = "FATAL",
  threshold = "info",
  logger = NULL
)

Arguments

trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal

Labels passed to logger_fn() for each level. They default to "TRACE", "DEBUG" and so on. Change them when the logging package names its levels differently, or uses objects.

threshold

The lowest level the built-in loggers write: one of "trace", "debug", "info", "warn", "error" or "fatal".

logger

An object a logging package needs to be passed, such as a log4r logger. Available to methods as class@logger.

class

A logger. Methods are dispatched on this argument.

level

The level label of the event, taken from the property of class named by the event's level, e.g. class@info.

msg

The message, a string.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

logger_fn() returns nothing useful. The others return a logger.

Details

  • logger_base is the base class. The default method prints LEVEL [timestamp]: message to the console.

  • logger_message writes the same LEVEL [timestamp]: message with message(), so it can be silenced with suppressMessages().

  • logger_fn(class, level, msg, ...) is the generic. Add a method to support any logging package, see extending_log.

logger_base and logger_message hide events below threshold. The trace events, such as the calls leading to an error, are below the default "info", so set threshold = "trace" to see them. A method for another logging package is free to ignore threshold and use that package's own.

Examples

logger_message()
#> <fnware::logger_message>
#>  @ trace    : chr "TRACE"
#>  @ debug    : chr "DEBUG"
#>  @ info     : chr "INFO"
#>  @ warn     : chr "WARN"
#>  @ error    : chr "ERROR"
#>  @ fatal    : chr "FATAL"
#>  @ threshold: chr "info"
#>  @ logger   : NULL
f := log_call(logger = logger_message()) %@% function(x) x
f(1)
#> INFO [2026-11-10T20:21:58.012Z]: Start f(x=1)
#> INFO [2026-11-10T20:21:58.012Z]: Finished f(x=1) Elapsed=00:00:00.000
#> [1] 1
